text:
sana: CI on main is red for e2e-integration (job: e2e/integration-linux). Looks like a KMS decrypt error after the key rotation window. Can someone triage?

sana: error snippet from the job:
```
Error: failed to decrypt secret SECRET_DB_PASSWORD: permission denied or invalid key version
caused by: googleapi: Error 403: Permission 'cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt' denied on resource projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/deploy-key/cryptoKeyVersions/5
```

mike: :eyes: likely the SA the runner uses lost the cryptoKeyDecrypter role when the key was rotated. Are we using the new key version alias? Which pipeline is using it?

sana: GitHub Actions self-hosted runner in infra pool. The env var SECRET_KMS_KEY points to projects/.../cryptoKeys/deploy-key (no version suffix). Rotation was automated last night.

alex: Quick checks: 1) confirm service account has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the key (or key ring) 2) check IAM policy for the specific key version 3) try a manual decrypt with gcloud as that SA.

mike: I'll run the IAM policy check now.

mike: ran: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy deploy-key --keyring=infra --location=global --project=redwood-prod`
Found: the `infra-runner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` binding is missing. Looks like our rotation script reapplied a restrictive policy.

mike: propose temporary workaround: add the binding back for the SA, retrigger CI. I'll add binding and then we can audit rotation script to avoid clobbering bindings.

sana: sounds good. Can you also run a bisect to confirm whether it started failing exactly after the rotation? If it's intermittent we might have a race.

mike: added binding with: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding deploy-key --keyring=infra --location=global --member=serviceAccount:infra-runner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`

ci-bot: Action required: job e2e/integration-linux has been re-run by mike. See: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/9876543

alex: rerunning with SKIP_CACHE=1 to avoid cached creds: `CI_ENV=prod SKIP_CACHE=1 ./scripts/ci-run.sh e2e/integration-linux`

ci-bot: Job succeeded ✅ (build 9876544) — all e2e tests passed.

kevin: nice catch. Next steps: 1) add integration test for rotation (ensure iam bindings preserved) 2) update rotation script to use `--preserve-iam` style logic / patch vs replace 3) add runbook entry so oncall knows to check key IAM after rotation. I'll file a GH issue and link.

sana: filing issue would be great. Thanks @mike for the quick fix. I'll follow up to make the rotation idempotent and update docs. :thumbsup:

mike: created GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/412 — added repro steps and commit patch idea.

sana: marking this resolved for now. If flakes recur re-open.
